8.14 Disturbance-specific historical kernels

Separate historical megamatrices are constructed for undisturbed and burned conditions. The same disturbance state is applied to all vital-rate functions in this initial implementation.

The flowering-stem-to-recruit relationship was fitted at the quadrat level. The mean number of flowering stems is therefore also calculated at the quadrat level separately for burned and unburned transitions.

Code 
pars_0 <- pars_mean
pars_0$fs_ref <- mean_stems_no_fire

pars_1 <- pars_mean
pars_1$fs_ref <- mean_stems_fire

# All mixture components use the same expected total flowering-stem production
# under the observed disturbance regime.
pars_regime <- pars_mean
pars_regime$fs_ref <- mean_stems_regime

K_0 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_0,
  disturbance = 0)$K_hist

K_1 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_1,
  disturbance = 1)$K_hist

K_regime_0 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_regime,
  disturbance = 0)$K_hist

K_regime_1 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_regime,
  disturbance = 1)$K_hist

K_regime <-
  p_0 * K_regime_0 +
  p_1 * K_regime_1

8.15 Projection of the historical population vector

The historical state vector contains two size distributions,

\[ \mathbf{N}_t = \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{n}_t \\ \mathbf{n}_{t-1} \end{pmatrix}. \]

For the mean IPM, both components are initialized using the mean observed size distribution. Thus, at the first projection,

\[ \mathbf{n}_{t-1} = \mathbf{n}_t = \bar{\mathbf{n}}. \]

This initialization implies that the first projected population is identical to that obtained from the corresponding ahistorical IPM because

\[ \mathbf{P}\mathbf{n}_t + \mathbf{F}\mathbf{n}_{t-1} = (\mathbf{P}+\mathbf{F})\mathbf{n}_t \]

when \(\mathbf{n}_{t-1}=\mathbf{n}_t\).

Only the upper half of the projected state vector represents the population at \(t+1\). The lower half is the stored population at \(t\) and must therefore not be counted as additional individuals.

Code 
project_kernel <- function(K, pars, label, df_init = df) {
  n <- as.integer(pars$mat_siz)
  n_current <- make_initial_n_mean(pars, df_init)
  n_previous <- n_current
  n_hist <- c(n_current, n_previous)

  h <- (pars$U - pars$L) / n
  n_initial <- sum(n_current) * h

  n_proj_hist <- K %*% n_hist
  n_next <- n_proj_hist[1:n]
  n_projected <- sum(n_next) * h

  tibble(
    lambda_type = label,
    asym_lambda = Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1]),
    proj_lambda = n_projected / n_initial,
    n_initial = n_initial,
    n_projected = n_projected)
}

The asymptotic growth rate is calculated from the complete historical megamatrix. In contrast, the one-step projected growth rate describes the change from the observed mean population distribution during the first projection. Because the initial current and historical size distributions are identical, the first projection is equivalent to the corresponding ahistorical projection. Historical effects emerge during subsequent iterations and in the asymptotic growth rate.

The historical asymptotic growth rates were approximately 0.956 under undisturbed conditions, 0.646 under fire, and 0.930 under the expected disturbance regime. All three values were below one, indicating declining long-term population growth under these deterministic mean conditions.

Code 
df_lambda_states <- bind_rows(
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_0,
    pars = pars_0,
    label = 'Undisturbed',
    disturbance = 0,
    p_state = p_0),
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_1,
    pars = pars_1,
    label = 'Fire',
    disturbance = 1,
    p_state = p_1))

recruits_ref_regime <-
  p_0 * predict_recruits_from_stems(
    flowering_stems = mean_stems_regime,
    pars = pars_regime,
    disturbance = 0) +
  p_1 * predict_recruits_from_stems(
    flowering_stems = mean_stems_regime,
    pars = pars_regime,
    disturbance = 1)

df_lambda_regime <- project_kernel(
  K = K_regime,
  pars = pars_regime,
  label = 'Expected disturbance regime') %>%
  mutate(
    disturbance = NA_real_,
    observed_state_probability = 1,
    flowering_stems_ref = mean_stems_regime,
    recruits_ref = recruits_ref_regime,
    recruits_per_stem = if_else(
      flowering_stems_ref > 0,
      recruits_ref / flowering_stems_ref,
      0))

df_lambda_mean <- bind_rows(
  df_lambda_states,

9 Historical environmenal projection model

The second historical IPM retains information about the disturbance environment experienced during the previous annual interval. This is necessary because fire affects different demographic processes over different time periods. Survival and growth from \(t\) to \(t+1\), as well as recruitment from flowering stems at \(t\) to recruits at \(t+1\), depend on disturbance during the current interval. In contrast, flowering probability and flowering-stem production at time \(t\) depend on disturbance during the preceding interval from \(t-1\) to \(t\).

The population state is therefore expanded according to previous disturbance history. Separate demographic kernels are constructed for each combination of previous and current fire,

\[ \mathbf{K}_{00},\quad \mathbf{K}_{01},\quad \mathbf{K}_{10},\quad \mathbf{K}_{11}, \]

and these are combined using the observed conditional probabilities of transitioning between disturbance states. This gives the environmental historical megamatrix

\[ \begin{pmatrix} p_{0|0}\mathbf{K}_{00} & p_{0|1}\mathbf{K}_{01} \\ p_{1|0}\mathbf{K}_{10} & p_{1|1}\mathbf{K}_{11} \end{pmatrix}. \]

The following chapter implements this formulation for Polygala lewtonii. Unlike the preceding time-lagged IPM, the additional state does not store the previous population vector. Instead, both components of the enlarged state vector represent individuals in the current population, separated according to whether the preceding interval was burned or unburned.

  mutate(
    disturbance = as.numeric(dist_transition),
    disturbance_prev = as.numeric(disturbance_prev),
    year = as.integer(year),
    site = factor(site)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !(year %in% v_years_re))

9.2 Vital-rate data

Survival and growth describe transitions from \(t\) to \(t+1\) and therefore use disturbance during the current interval. Flowering probability and flowering-stem production are measured at time \(t\) and use disturbance during the preceding interval from \(t-1\) to \(t\). Recruitment links flowering stems at \(t\) to recruits at \(t+1\) and again uses disturbance during the current interval. ### Survival

Code 
df_su <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(survives),
    size_t0 != 0,
    is.finite(logvol_t0),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_2),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_3),
    !is.na(disturbance)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    id, site, year, size_t0, survives, size_t1,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t1, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3,
    volume_t0, volume_t1, logvol_t0, logvol_t1,
    logvol_t0_2, logvol_t0_3, disturbance, stage)

###Grwoth

Code 
df_gr <- df %>%
  filter(
    size_t0 != 0,
    size_t1 != 0,
    is.finite(logvol_t0),
    is.finite(logvol_t1),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_2),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_3),
    !is.na(disturbance)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    id, site, year, size_t0, size_t1,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t1, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3,
    volume_t0, volume_t1, logvol_t0, logvol_t1,
    logvol_t0_2, logvol_t0_3, disturbance, stage)

###Flower

Code 
# Recruits are retained because some observed recruits flowered.
df_fl <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(flower),
    is.finite(logvol_t0),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_2),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_3),
    !is.na(disturbance_prev)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    id, site, year, size_t0, flower, fl_nr, size_t1,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t1, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3,
    volume_t0, volume_t1, logvol_t0, logvol_t1,
    logvol_t0_2, logvol_t0_3, disturbance_prev, stage, recruits)

df_fl_cond <- df_fl %>%
  filter(
    flower == 1,
    !is.na(fl_nr),
    fl_nr > 0,
    fl_nr == round(fl_nr))

9.2.1 Flowering stems to recruits

Code 
# Total flowering stems in quadrat q during year t predict recruits in the
# same quadrat during year t + 1. Current fire is included as a quadrat-level
# fixed effect.
df_quad_year_sampled <- df %>%
  distinct(site, quad, year)

df_fs2r <- df %>%
  group_by(site, quad, year) %>%
  summarise(
    fs_t0 = sum(fl_nr, na.rm = TRUE),
    disturbance = if_else(
      all(is.na(disturbance)),
      NA_real_,
      max(disturbance, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = year + 1) %>%
  semi_join(
    df_quad_year_sampled %>%
      transmute(
        site,
        quad,
        year_t1 = year),
    by = c(
      "site",
      "quad",
      "year_t1")) %>%
  left_join(
    df %>%
      filter(recruits == 1) %>%
      count(
        site,
        quad,
        year,
        name = "re_t1"),
    by = c(
      "site",
      "quad",
      "year_t1" = "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    re_t1 = replace_na(re_t1, 0L),
    site = factor(site),
    fs_t0_log = log1p(fs_t0),
    re_t1_log = log1p(re_t1)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(year_t1),
    !is.na(disturbance),
    !(year %in% v_years_re),
    !(year_t1 %in% v_years_re))

9.4 Mean vital-rate plots

Code 
make_mean_prediction <- function(data, model, disturbance_var) {
  x <- seq(
    min(data$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(data$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = 200)
  
  pred <- expand_grid(
    logvol_t0 = x,
    disturbance_value = c(0, 1)) %>%
    mutate(
      logvol_t0_2 = logvol_t0^2,
      logvol_t0_3 = logvol_t0^3,
      disturbance_plot = factor(
        disturbance_value,
        levels = c(0, 1),
        labels = c('No fire', 'Fire')))
  
  pred[[disturbance_var]] <- pred$disturbance_value
  pred$prediction <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = pred,
    type = 'response')
  
  pred
}

make_mean_plot <- function(
    data, model, response, disturbance_var, title, y_lab,
    probability = FALSE) {
  pred <- make_mean_prediction(
    data = data,
    model = model,
    disturbance_var = disturbance_var)
  
  data_plot <- data %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance_plot = factor(
        .data[[disturbance_var]],
        levels = c(0, 1),
        labels = c('No fire', 'Fire')))
  
  point_layer <- if (probability) {
    geom_jitter(
      data = data_plot,
      aes(
        x = logvol_t0,
        y = .data[[response]],
        color = disturbance_plot),
      alpha = 0.15,
      size = 0.7,
      width = 0.05,
      height = 0.05)
  } else {
    geom_point(
      data = data_plot,
      aes(
        x = logvol_t0,
        y = .data[[response]],
        color = disturbance_plot),
      alpha = 0.15,
      size = 0.7)
  }
  
  p <- ggplot() +
    point_layer +
    geom_line(
      data = pred,
      aes(
        x = logvol_t0,
        y = prediction,
        color = disturbance_plot),
      linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c('No fire' = 'black', 'Fire' = 'red')) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
      x = expression('log(volume)'[t0]),
      y = y_lab,
      color = NULL)
  
  if (probability) {
    p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))
  }
  
  p
}

9.6 Parameter extraction

Code 
size_term_map <- c(
  b0 = '(Intercept)',
  b1 = 'logvol_t0',
  b2 = 'logvol_t0_2',
  b3 = 'logvol_t0_3',
  bd = 'disturbance')

lagged_size_term_map <- c(
  b0 = '(Intercept)',
  b1 = 'logvol_t0',
  b2 = 'logvol_t0_2',
  b3 = 'logvol_t0_3',
  bd = 'disturbance_prev')

extract_terms <- function(model, prefix, term_map) {
  coefs <- stats::coef(model)
  
  values <- vapply(term_map, function(term_i) {
    if (term_i %in% names(coefs)) {
      unname(coefs[[term_i]])
    } else {
      0
    }
  }, numeric(1))
  
  names(values) <- paste0(prefix, names(term_map))
  values
}

extract_coef <- function(model, term, default = 0) {
  coefs <- stats::coef(model)
  
  if (term %in% names(coefs)) {
    unname(coefs[[term]])
  } else {
    default
  }
}

grow_var_coef <- stats::coef(mod_gr_var)

  c(
    df_gr$logvol_t0,
    df_gr$logvol_t1,
    df_recr$logvol_t0),
  na.rm = TRUE,
  finite = TRUE)
mesh_limits <- c(mesh_limits[1] - 0.1, mesh_limits[2] + 0.1)

  extract_terms(mod_su_best, 'surv_', size_term_map),
  extract_terms(mod_gr_best, 'grow_', size_term_map),
  extract_terms(mod_fl_best, 'fl_', lagged_size_term_map),

9.7 IPM functions

The fitted model coefficients are translated into continuous demographic functions for survival, growth, flowering, flowering-stem production, and recruitment. Importantly, the distinction between current and previous disturbance is retained: survival and growth depend on disturbance, while flowering and flowering-stem production depend on disturbance_prev. Recruitment combines flowering-stem production at \(t\) with the effect of current disturbance on recruitment from \(t\) to \(t+1\).

Code 
get_par <- function(pars, par_name, default = 0) {
  if (!is.null(pars[[par_name]])) {
    pars[[par_name]]
  } else {
    default
  }
}

vital_lp <- function(x, pars, prefix, disturbance = 0) {
  get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'b0')) +
    get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'b1')) * x +
    get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'b2')) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'b3')) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'bd')) * disturbance
}


# Survival ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sx <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  plogis(vital_lp(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    prefix = 'surv_',
    disturbance = disturbance))
}


# Growth -----------------------------------------------------------------------
grow_mu <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  vital_lp(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    prefix = 'grow_',
    disturbance = disturbance)
}

grow_sd <- function(mean_value, pars) {
  variance <- get_par(pars, 'grow_var_a') *
    exp(get_par(pars, 'grow_var_b') * mean_value)
  
  sqrt(pmax(variance, .Machine$double.eps))
}

gxy <- function(x, y, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  mean_value <- grow_mu(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  sd_value <- grow_sd(
    mean_value = mean_value,
    pars = pars)
  
  dnorm(y, mean = mean_value, sd = sd_value)
}


# Flowering probability --------------------------------------------------------
fl_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  plogis(vital_lp(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    prefix = 'fl_',
    disturbance = disturbance_prev))
}


# Flowering-stem number conditional on flowering ------------------------------
fln_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  exp(vital_lp(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    prefix = 'fln_',
    disturbance = disturbance_prev))
}


# Expected flowering stems per individual ------------------------------------
fs_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  fl_x(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev) *
    fln_x(
      x = x,
      pars = pars,
      disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
}


# Flowering-stem-to-recruit conversion ----------------------------------------
predict_recruits_from_stems <- function(
    flowering_stems, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  stems_nonnegative <- pmax(flowering_stems, 0)
  
  slope <- get_par(pars, 're_b1') +
    get_par(pars, 're_bf') * disturbance
  
  eta <- get_par(pars, 're_b0') +
    get_par(pars, 're_bd') * disturbance +
    slope * log1p(stems_nonnegative)
  
  recruits <- expm1(
    eta + 0.5 * get_par(pars, 're_sigma')^2)
  
  pmax(recruits, 0)
}

recruits_per_stem <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  fs_ref <- get_par(pars, 'fs_ref', 0)
  
  if (!is.finite(fs_ref) || fs_ref <= 0) {
    return(0)
  }
  
  predict_recruits_from_stems(
    flowering_stems = fs_ref,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance) / fs_ref
}

rx <- function(
    x, pars, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  fs_x(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev) *
    recruits_per_stem(
      pars = pars,
      disturbance = disturbance)
}


# Recruit size distribution ----------------------------------------------------
recr_y <- function(y, pars) {
  dnorm(
    y,
    mean = get_par(pars, 'recr_mean'),
    sd = get_par(pars, 'recr_sd'))
}


# Fertility matrix -------------------------------------------------------------
fy <- function(
    y, x, pars, h, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  Pvec <- recr_y(y, pars)
  recruit_mass <- sum(Pvec * h)
  
  if (!is.finite(recruit_mass) || recruit_mass <= 0) {
    stop('Recruit size distribution has no mass inside the mesh')
  }
  
  Pvec <- Pvec / recruit_mass
  
  Rvec <- rx(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
  
  outer(Pvec, Rvec) * h
}

9.8 Kernel

For a specified combination of current and previous disturbance, the demographic functions are combined into a size-structured projection kernel. The survival-growth component describes the contribution of individuals at size \(x\) at time \(t\) to surviving individuals of size \(y\) at \(t+1\), while the fecundity component describes the contribution of those individuals to new recruits. Because flowering depends on previous disturbance whereas survival, growth, and recruitment depend on current disturbance, the resulting kernel is conditional on both disturbance states.

Code 
kernel <- function(
    pars, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  n <- as.integer(pars$mat_siz)
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  Fmat <- fy(
    y = y,
    x = y,
    pars = pars,
    h = h,
    disturbance = disturbance,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
  
  Smat <- sx(
    x = y,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  Gmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  Gmat[] <- t(
    outer(
      y,
      y,
      Vectorize(function(x, y) {
        gxy(
          x = x,
          y = y,
          pars = pars,
          disturbance = disturbance)
      }))) * h
  
  Tmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  
  for (i in 1:(n / 2)) {
    Gmat[1, i] <- Gmat[1, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    Tmat[, i] <- Gmat[, i] * Smat[i]
  }
  
  for (i in (n / 2 + 1):n) {
    Gmat[n, i] <- Gmat[n, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    Tmat[, i] <- Gmat[, i] * Smat[i]
  }
  
  k_yx <- Fmat + Tmat
  
  list(
    k_yx = k_yx,
    Fmat = Fmat,
    Tmat = Tmat,
    Gmat = Gmat,
    Smat = Smat,
    meshpts = y,
    h = h)
}

lambda_ipm <- function(
    pars, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  K <- kernel(
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)$k_yx
  
  Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1])
}

9.9 Mean observed size distribution

A mean observed population size distribution is used as the initial size-structured population vector. Annual size-frequency distributions are first constructed from the observed plants and then averaged across years. Recruits without a usable size measurement are distributed according to the fitted recruit-size distribution.

Code 
# The vector is the arithmetic mean of annual size-frequency vectors. Unsized
# recruits are distributed over the fitted recruit-size distribution.
make_initial_n_mean <- function(pars, df_init = df) {
  n <- as.integer(pars$mat_siz)
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  breaks <- seq(L, U, length.out = n + 1)
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  recruit_density <- recr_y(y, pars)
  recruit_density <- recruit_density / sum(recruit_density * h)
  
  years_i <- df_init %>%
    filter(!is.na(year)) %>%
    distinct(year) %>%
    arrange(year) %>%
    pull(year)
  
  counts_by_year <- purrr::map(years_i, function(year_i) {
    df_i <- df_init %>%
      filter(year == year_i)
    
    x <- df_i %>%
      filter(is.finite(logvol_t0)) %>%
      pull(logvol_t0)
    
    size_counts <- hist(
      pmin(pmax(x, L), U),
      breaks = breaks,
      plot = FALSE,
      include.lowest = TRUE)$counts
    
    n_unsized_recruits <- df_i %>%
      summarise(
        n = sum(
          !is.finite(logvol_t0) & recruits == 1,
          na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      pull(n)
    
    size_counts + n_unsized_recruits * recruit_density * h
  })
  
  mean_counts <- Reduce(`+`, counts_by_year) / length(counts_by_year)
  mean_counts / h
}

Code 
# Each sampled quadrat-year receives equal weight. Current disturbance refers
# to the interval t -> t + 1 and previous disturbance to t - 1 -> t.
df_disturbance_regime <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(quad),
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(disturbance),
    !is.na(disturbance_prev)) %>%
  distinct(
    quad,
    year,
    disturbance,
    disturbance_prev) %>%
  count(
    disturbance,
    disturbance_prev,
    name = 'n_quadrat_years') %>%
  complete(
    disturbance = c(0, 1),
    disturbance_prev = c(0, 1),
    fill = list(n_quadrat_years = 0)) %>%
  arrange(
    disturbance_prev,
    disturbance)

9.11 Disturbance transition probabilities

The environmental historical model requires not only the frequency of fire, but also information on how fire states follow one another through time. Disturbance is therefore represented by two states: disturbance_prev, describing fire during \(t-1\) to \(t\), and disturbance, describing fire during \(t\) to \(t+1\). Together they define four possible disturbance histories: no fire in either interval, current fire only, previous fire only, or fire in both intervals.

The observed quadrat-year histories are used to estimate conditional disturbance-transition probabilities,

\[ P(D_t \mid D_{t-1}), \]

which determine the probability of entering each current disturbance state given the disturbance state during the preceding interval.

Four demographic kernels are consequently required,

\[ \mathbf{K}{00},\quad \mathbf{K}{01},\quad \mathbf{K}{10},\quad \mathbf{K}{11}, \]

where the first subscript denotes current disturbance and the second denotes previous disturbance. These kernels are combined with the conditional disturbance-transition probabilities to form the environmental historical megamatrix,

\[ \mathbf{K}{\mathrm{env}} = \begin{pmatrix} p{0|0}\mathbf{K}{00} & p{0|1}\mathbf{K}{01} \ p{1|0}\mathbf{K}{10} & p{1|1}\mathbf{K}_{11} \end{pmatrix}. \]

With 200 size classes for each previous-disturbance state, the resulting historical projection matrix has dimensions \(400 \times 400\).

\[ P(D_t \mid D_{t-1}). \]

These probabilities describe how likely each current disturbance state is given the disturbance state experienced during the preceding interval.

Code 
# Environmental transitions are conditional probabilities:
# P(disturbance_t | disturbance_t-1).
df_disturbance_transition <- df_disturbance_regime %>%
  group_by(disturbance_prev) %>%
  mutate(
    p_transition = n_quadrat_years /
      sum(n_quadrat_years)) %>%
  ungroup()

df_disturbance_transition

get_transition_probability <- function(
    disturbance_i, disturbance_prev_i) {
  df_disturbance_transition %>%
    filter(
      disturbance == disturbance_i,
      disturbance_prev == disturbance_prev_i) %>%
    pull(p_transition)
}

p_1_given_0 <- get_transition_probability(1, 0)

p_1_given_1 <- get_transition_probability(1, 1)

    p_previous = n_quadrat_years /

9.12 State-specific demographic kernels

Because the vital rates depend on different disturbance intervals, a separate demographic kernel is constructed for each combination of previous and current disturbance. The first index denotes disturbance during the current transition from \(t\) to \(t+1\), while the second denotes disturbance during the preceding transition from \(t-1\) to \(t\).

Thus, the four kernels are

\[ \mathbf{K}{00},\quad \mathbf{K}{01},\quad \mathbf{K}{10},\quad \mathbf{K}{11}, \]

where, for example, \(\mathbf{K}_{10}\) represents demographic transitions under current fire following an unburned previous interval.

Code 
# First digit  = current disturbance, t -> t + 1.
# Second digit = previous disturbance, t - 1 -> t.
K_00 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_prev_0,
  disturbance = 0,
  disturbance_prev = 0)$k_yx

K_01 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_prev_1,
  disturbance = 0,
  disturbance_prev = 1)$k_yx

K_10 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_prev_0,
  disturbance = 1,
  disturbance_prev = 0)$k_yx

K_11 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_prev_1,
  disturbance = 1,
  disturbance_prev = 1)$k_yx


# Environmental historical megamatrix ----------------------------------------
# Columns represent disturbance during t - 1 -> t.
# Rows represent disturbance during t -> t + 1.
K_env_hist <- rbind(
  cbind(
    p_0_given_0 * K_00,
    p_0_given_1 * K_01),
  cbind(
    p_1_given_0 * K_10,
    p_1_given_1 * K_11))


# Environmental historical asymptotic lambda ----------------------------------
lambda_env_hist <- Re(
  eigen(
    K_env_hist,
    only.values = TRUE)$values[1])

lambda_env_hist
## [1] 0.9259645

9.13 Asymptotic and projected lambda

Population growth is evaluated both for the four individual disturbance-history kernels and for the complete environmental historical model. The asymptotic growth rate is obtained from the dominant eigenvalue of the respective projection matrix, whereas the projected growth rate describes the change in abundance during a single projection from the observed mean size distribution.

For the environmental historical model, the initial 200-element size distribution is divided between the two previous-disturbance states according to their observed frequencies. The two components therefore represent different parts of the same population and together retain the original total abundance.

Code 
# Mean observed size distribution used for the four fixed environmental states.
n_obs <- make_initial_n_mean(pars_mean)

n <- as.integer(pars_mean$mat_siz)
h <- (pars_mean$U - pars_mean$L) / n

# For the environmental historical IPM, the observed population is divided
# between the two previous-disturbance states. The two blocks are mutually
# exclusive parts of the same population and therefore must not be duplicated.
n_env_initial <- c(
  p_prev_0 * n_obs,
  p_prev_1 * n_obs)


# General projection function -------------------------------------------------
project_kernel <- function(K, n_initial, h, label) {
  n_initial_total <- sum(n_initial) * h
  
  n_proj <- as.numeric(K %*% n_initial)
  n_projected <- sum(n_proj) * h
  
  tibble(
    lambda_type = label,
    asym_lambda = Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1]),
    proj_lambda = n_projected / n_initial_total,
    n_initial = n_initial_total,
    n_projected = n_projected)
}


# Fixed disturbance-state lambdas ---------------------------------------------
make_state_lambda <- function(
    K, label, disturbance, disturbance_prev) {
  project_kernel(
    K = K,
    n_initial = n_obs,
    h = h,
    label = label) %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance = disturbance,
      disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
}

df_lambda_states <- bind_rows(
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_00,
    label = 'Undisturbed',
    disturbance = 0,
    disturbance_prev = 0),
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_10,
    label = 'Current-year fire',
    disturbance = 1,
    disturbance_prev = 0),
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_01,
    label = 'Previous-year fire',
    disturbance = 0,
    disturbance_prev = 1),
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_11,
    label = 'Fire in both years',
    disturbance = 1,
    disturbance_prev = 1))


# Environmental historical regime --------------------------------------------
df_lambda_env_hist <- project_kernel(
  K = K_env_hist,
  n_initial = n_env_initial,
  h = h,
  label = 'Environmental historical regime') %>%
  mutate(
    disturbance = NA_real_,
    disturbance_prev = NA_real_)


# Combined lambda table --------------------------------------------------------
df_lambda_env <- bind_rows(
  df_lambda_states,
  df_lambda_env_hist)

## # ℹ 1 more variable: disturbance_prev <dbl>

9.14 Observed annual abundance change

Observed population growth is calculated independently from the IPM using annual changes in abundance. Only quadrats represented in both consecutive years are retained so that abundance at \(t\) and \(t+1\) refers to the same set of sampling units. Annual population growth is then calculated as

\[ \lambda_t = \frac{N_{t+1}}{N_t}. \]

Because population growth is multiplicative through time, the geometric mean of annual \(\lambda_t\) values is used as the summary measure of observed population growth across the study period.

Code 
# Counts include sized plants and recruits without a usable size measurement.
# Only quadrats with individual records in both consecutive years are retained.
df_counts_quad_year <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(site),
    !is.na(quad),
    !is.na(year)) %>%
  group_by(site, quad, year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sized = sum(
      is.finite(logvol_t0),
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unsized_recruits = sum(
      !is.finite(logvol_t0) & recruits == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t0 = n_sized + n_unsized_recruits,
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(site, quad, year) %>%
  group_by(site, quad) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    n_t1 = lead(n_t0),
    year_gap = year_t1 - year) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(year_gap == 1)

df_obs_growth_year <- df_counts_quad_year %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_t0 = sum(n_t0),
    n_t1 = sum(n_t1),
    n_quadrats = n(),
    n_sites = n_distinct(site),
    obs_lambda = n_t1 / n_t0,
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_t0 > 0)

9.15 Observed and modeled population growth through time

Model-based population growth is compared with population change observed directly in the monitoring data. Annual abundance changes are calculated from quadrats sampled in both consecutive years so that abundance at \(t\) and \(t+1\) refers to the same sampling units.

For each annual transition, observed population growth is calculated as

\[ \lambda_t = \frac{N_{t+1}}{N_t}. \]

Because population growth compounds multiplicatively through time, the geometric mean of the annual growth rates is used to describe mean observed population growth across the monitoring period.

Code

    proj_lambda) %>%
  pivot_longer(

      proj_lambda),
    names_to = 'metric',
    values_to = 'lambda') %>%
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      asym_lambda = 'Asymptotic',
      proj_lambda = 'One-step projected'))

10 Yearly historical kuss projection model

10.1 Introduction

This analysis develops a year-specific historical integral projection model (IPM) for Polygala lewtonii at Archbold. The model combines annual variation in demographic rates with the delayed contribution of reproduction to recruitment.

Survival, growth, flowering, flowering-stem production, and recruitment are first modeled separately. Year-specific demographic variation is introduced through the year effects from the fitted mixed models. This means that each annual IPM uses the demographic conditions estimated for that particular year, rather than applying one mean set of vital-rate parameters to the full time series.

Disturbance is incorporated as a single common fire state within the IPM. Survival, growth, flowering, flowering-stem production, and recruitment are therefore evaluated under either

  • no disturbance (disturbance = 0), or
  • disturbance (disturbance = 1).

This deliberately places disturbance on the same level for all demographic processes inside the IPM. The underlying flowering and flower-number models are still fitted using previous-year disturbance, as in the original demographic models, but their disturbance coefficients are applied to the common disturbance state when the IPM is constructed.

The historical structure is needed because flowering in year \(t\) contributes to recruitment in year \(t+1\). The population state therefore contains both the current and previous size distributions,

\[ \mathbf{n}^{H}_t = \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{n}_t \\ \mathbf{n}_{t-1} \end{pmatrix}. \]

The corresponding historical kernel is

\[ \mathbf{K}^{H}_t = \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{T}_t & \mathbf{F}_t \\ \mathbf{I} & \mathbf{0} \end{pmatrix}, \]

where \(\mathbf{T}_t\) contains survival and growth, \(\mathbf{F}_t\) contains fertility, \(\mathbf{I}\) transfers the current population into the lagged state, and \(\mathbf{0}\) prevents the lagged state from persisting beyond one year. Projection therefore gives

\[ \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{n}_{t+1} \\ \mathbf{n}_t \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{T}_t & \mathbf{F}_t \\ \mathbf{I} & \mathbf{0} \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{n}_t \\ \mathbf{n}_{t-1} \end{pmatrix}. \]

For the year-specific model, a separate historical kernel is constructed for each year using that year’s demographic parameters. For every year, two asymptotic scenarios are evaluated: one assuming no fire and one assuming fire. The dominant eigenvalue of the corresponding historical kernel gives the year-specific asymptotic population growth rate under that disturbance state.

The yearly model is also used for one-step projections of the observed population. For each quadrat-year transition, the observed size distribution in year \(t\) is combined with the observed size distribution from year \(t-1\). The historical kernel for year \(t\), using the observed disturbance state of that quadrat, is then applied once to obtain the predicted population in year \(t+1\).

The projected population growth rate is calculated as

\[ \lambda_{\mathrm{proj},t} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{projected},t+1}} {N_{\mathrm{observed},t}}. \]

This differs from the asymptotic growth rate. The projected lambda depends on the actual observed population structure in years \(t\) and \(t-1\), whereas the asymptotic lambda is determined by the dominant eigenvalue of the annual historical kernel and represents the long-term growth rate that would result if the demographic conditions and disturbance state of that year were held constant.

Observed population growth from \(t\) to \(t+1\) is then compared with both the projected and asymptotic growth rates. This allows the year-specific model to be evaluated against the realized annual population dynamics while retaining the historical lag between flowering and recruitment.

10.3 Vital rates

10.3.1 Survival

Code 
df_su <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(survives),
    size_t0 != 0,
    is.finite(logvol_t0),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_2),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_3),
    !is.na(disturbance)) %>%
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    disturbance = factor(disturbance, levels = c(0, 1))) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    id, site, year, size_t0, survives, size_t1,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t1, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3,
    volume_t0, volume_t1, logvol_t0, logvol_t1,
    logvol_t0_2, logvol_t0_3,
    disturbance, stage)


# Survival model ---------------------------------------------------------------
mod_su_0 <- glmer(
  survives ~ disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_10 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_11 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_20 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_21 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_30 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + logvol_t0_3 +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_31 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + logvol_t0_3 + disturbance +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)


mods_su <- list(
  mod_su_0, mod_su_10, mod_su_11, 
  mod_su_20, mod_su_21, mod_su_30, mod_su_31)
mods_su_dAIC <- bbmle::AICctab(mods_su, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAIC
mods_su_sorted <- order(mods_su_dAIC)

if (length(v_mod_set_su) == 0) {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- mods_su_sorted[1]
  v_mod_su_index <- mod_su_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_su + 1
  v_mod_su_index <- v_mod_set_su
}

mod_su_best <- mods_su[[mod_su_index_bestfit]]
mod_su_ranef <- coef(mod_su_best)$year

mod_su_best

# Survival plots by year -------------------------------------------------------
make_su_year_plot <- function(year_i) {
  df_i <- df_su %>% filter(year == year_i)
  
  x <- seq(
    min(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)
  
  pred_i <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    logvol_t0 = x,
    disturbance = levels(df_su$disturbance)) %>%
    mutate(
      logvol_t0_2 = logvol_t0^2,
      logvol_t0_3 = logvol_t0^3,
      disturbance = factor(
        disturbance, levels = levels(df_su$disturbance)),
      year = factor(year_i, levels = levels(df_su$year)))
  
  pred_i$survives <- predict(
    mod_su_best, newdata = pred_i,
    type = "response", re.form = NULL)
  
  pts_i <- df_i %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(logvol_t0, breaks = 8)) %>%
    group_by(bin, disturbance) %>%
    summarise(
      logvol_t0 = mean(logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
      survives = mean(survives, na.rm = TRUE),
      n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(!is.na(logvol_t0), n > 0)
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = pts_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, survives, color = disturbance), size = 1.1) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, survives, color = disturbance,
          linetype = disturbance),
      linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "black", "1" = "red")) +
    labs(
      title = year_i,
      x = expression("log(volume)"[t0]),
      y = expression("Survival probability"[t1])) +
    ylim(0, 1) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 5), legend.position = "none")
}

  df_i <- df_gr %>% filter(year == year_i)
  x <- seq(min(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
           max(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)
  pred_i <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    logvol_t0 = x,
    disturbance = levels(df_gr$disturbance)) %>%
    mutate(
      logvol_t0_2 = logvol_t0^2,
      logvol_t0_3 = logvol_t0^3,
      disturbance = factor(
        disturbance, levels = levels(df_gr$disturbance)),
      year = factor(year_i, levels = levels(df_gr$year)))
  
  pred_i <- pred_i %>%
    mutate(
      logvol_t1 = predict(
        mod_gr_best,
        newdata = pred_i,
        re.form = NULL))
  pts_i <- df_i %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(logvol_t0, breaks = 8)) %>%
    group_by(bin, disturbance) %>%
    summarise(
      logvol_t0 = mean(logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
      logvol_t1 = mean(logvol_t1, na.rm = TRUE),
      n = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    filter(!is.na(logvol_t0), n > 0)
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = pts_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, logvol_t1, color = disturbance),
      size = 1.1) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, logvol_t1, color = disturbance,
          linetype = disturbance),
      linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = 'blue', lty = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c('0' = 'black', '1' = 'red')) +
    labs(
      title = year_i,
      x = expression('log(volume)'[t0]),
      y = expression('log(volume)'[t1])) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 5), legend.position = 'none')
}

gr_yrs <- lapply(levels(df_gr$year), make_gr_year_plot)
fig_gr_years <- wrap_plots(gr_yrs) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = 'Growth - year specific',
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = 'bold'),

# Growth variance --------------------------------------------------------------
mod_gr_x <- fitted(mod_gr_best)
mod_gr_y <- resid(mod_gr_best)^2
mod_gr_var <- nls(
  mod_gr_y ~ a * exp(b * mod_gr_x),
  start = list(a = 1, b = 0),
  control = nls.control(maxiter = 1000, tol = 1e-6, warnOnly = TRUE))

# Flowering stems to recruits --------------------------------------------------
# Total flowering stems in quadrat q during year t predict recruits in the
# same quadrat during year t + 1. Current fire is retained at the quadrat level.
df_quad_year_sampled <- df %>%
  distinct(
    site,
    quad,
    year)

df_fs2r <- df %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    quad,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    fs_t0 = sum(
      fl_nr,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    disturbance = first(
      disturbance[!is.na(disturbance)],
      default = NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = year + 1) %>%
  semi_join(
    df_quad_year_sampled %>%
      transmute(
        site,
        quad,
        year_t1 = year),
    by = c(
      'site',
      'quad',
      'year_t1')) %>%
  left_join(
    df %>%
      filter(recruits == 1) %>%
      count(
        site,
        quad,
        year,
        name = 're_t1'),
    by = c(
      'site',
      'quad',
      'year_t1' = 'year')) %>%
  mutate(
    re_t1 = replace_na(re_t1, 0L),
    fs_t0_log = log1p(fs_t0),
    re_t1_log = log1p(re_t1)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(year_t1),
    !is.na(disturbance),
    !(year %in% v_years_re),
    !(year_t1 %in% v_years_re)) %>%
  mutate(
    site = factor(site),
    year_t0 = factor(year),
    year_t1 = factor(year_t1),
    disturbance_t0 = factor(
      disturbance,
      levels = c(0, 1)))

# Keep the old mean-script recruitment plot as a quick check.
fig_fs2r_raw <- ggplot(
  df_fs2r,
  aes(x = fs_t0, y = re_t1, color = disturbance_t0)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.2, width = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('0' = 'black', '1' = 'red')) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = 'Recruits t1 by flowering stems t0',
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    x = 'Total flowering stems in quadrat in year t',
    y = 'Number of recruits in quadrat in year t + 1',
    color = 'Fire')

  optimizer = 'bobyqa',
  optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

  mutate(
    disturbance =

  re_t1_log ~ 1 +
    (1 | year_t1),
  data = df_fs2r,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = ctrl_re)

# Disturbance only

  re_t1_log ~ disturbance +
    (1 | year_t1),
  data = df_fs2r,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = ctrl_re)

predict_re_safe <- function(model, newdata, re.form = NULL) {
  if (inherits(model, 'merMod')) {
    out <- predict(
      model, newdata = newdata, re.form = re.form, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
  } else {
    out <- predict(model, newdata = newdata)
  }
  return(out)
}

make_re_year_plot <- function(year_i) {
  df_i <- df_fs2r %>% filter(year_t1 == year_i)

    0, max(df_i$fs_t0_log, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)
  
  pred_i <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    fs_t0_log = x,
    disturbance_t0 = levels(df_fs2r$disturbance_t0)) %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance =
        as.numeric(as.character(disturbance_t0)),
      year_t1 = factor(year_i, levels = levels(df_fs2r$year_t1)),
      disturbance_t0 = factor(
        disturbance_t0, levels = levels(df_fs2r$disturbance_t0)))
  
  pred_i <- pred_i %>%
    mutate(
      pred_re = predict_re_safe(
        mod_re_best, pred_i, re.form = NULL))
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = df_i,
      aes(fs_t0_log, re_t1_log, color = site, shape = site),
      alpha = 0.75, size = 2) +
    geom_line(

      inherit.aes = FALSE, color = 'black', linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_color_viridis_d(option = 'turbo', end = 0.95) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = site_shapes_re) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c('0' = 'solid', '1' = 'dashed')) +
    theme_bw() +

10.4 Parameter extraction

# Parameter extraction helpers -------------------------------------------------
empty_coef_df <- function() {
  data.frame(coefficient = character(), value = numeric())
}

is_mixed_model <- function(model) {
  inherits(model, 'merMod')
}

get_fixef_safe <- function(model) {
  if (is_mixed_model(model)) {
    fixef(model)
  } else {
    coef(model)
  }
}

get_group_coef_safe <- function(model, group_var) {
  if (!is_mixed_model(model)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  coef_list <- coef(model)
  if (!(group_var %in% names(coef_list))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  coef_list[[group_var]]
}

find_model_term <- function(model_terms, aliases) {
  aliases <- unlist(aliases)
  for (alias in aliases) {
    if (grepl('^regex:', alias)) {
      pattern <- sub('^regex:', '', alias)
      hit <- grep(pattern, model_terms, value = TRUE)
    } else {
      hit <- model_terms[model_terms == alias]
    }
    if (length(hit) > 0) {
      return(hit[1])
    }
  }
  NA_character_
}

bind_coef_rows <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!vapply(x, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  out <- do.call(rbind, x)
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

check_duplicate_coefficients <- function(x, object_name = 'parameter table') {
  dup <- x$coefficient[duplicated(x$coefficient)]
  if (length(dup) > 0) {
    stop(
      object_name,
      ' contains duplicated coefficient names: ',
      paste(unique(dup), collapse = ', '))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

coef_df_to_list <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) == 0) {
    return(list())
  }
  check_duplicate_coefficients(x)
  x %>%
    mutate(coefficient = as.character(coefficient)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = coefficient, values_from = value) %>%
    as.list()
}

extract_fixed_pars <- function(model, term_map, fill_missing = TRUE) {
  model_coefs <- get_fixef_safe(model)
  model_terms <- names(model_coefs)
  out <- lapply(names(term_map), function(coef_name) {
    model_term <- find_model_term(model_terms, term_map[[coef_name]])
    if (is.na(model_term)) {
      if (fill_missing) {
        value <- 0
      } else {
        return(NULL)
      }
    } else {
      value <- unname(model_coefs[model_term])
    }
    data.frame(coefficient = coef_name, value = value)
  })
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}

extract_group_pars <- function(model, group_var, term_map, fill_missing = TRUE) {
  coef_matrix <- get_group_coef_safe(model, group_var)
  if (is.null(coef_matrix)) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  model_terms <- colnames(coef_matrix)
  out <- lapply(names(term_map), function(coef_prefix) {
    model_term <- find_model_term(model_terms, term_map[[coef_prefix]])
    if (is.na(model_term)) {
      if (fill_missing) {
        value <- rep(0, nrow(coef_matrix))
      } else {
        return(NULL)
      }
    } else {
      value <- coef_matrix[, model_term]
    }
    data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0(coef_prefix, '_', rownames(coef_matrix)),
      value = value)
  })
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}

extract_re_ranef_devs <- function(model, group_var, group_label) {
  if (!inherits(model, 'merMod')) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  ranef_list <- ranef(model)
  if (!(group_var %in% names(ranef_list))) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  ranef_matrix <- ranef_list[[group_var]]
  out <- list()
  if ('(Intercept)' %in% colnames(ranef_matrix)) {
    out[['intercept']] <- data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0('re_u0_', group_label, '_',
                           rownames(ranef_matrix)),
      value = ranef_matrix[, '(Intercept)'])
  }
  if ('fs_t0_log' %in% colnames(ranef_matrix)) {
    out[['slope']] <- data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0('re_u1_', group_label, '_',
                           rownames(ranef_matrix)),
      value = ranef_matrix[, 'fs_t0_log'])
  }
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}

10.5 IPM helper functions

Code 
inv_logit <- function(x) {
  plogis(x)
}

get_par <- function(pars, par_name, default = 0) {
  if (!is.null(pars[[par_name]])) {
    return(pars[[par_name]])
  }
  default
}

make_ipm_pars <- function(
    pars_mean,
    pars_year = NULL,
    pars_re_year_t1 = NULL,
    year = NULL,
    re_year_t1 = NULL) {
  pars <- pars_mean
  
  if (!is.null(year) && !is.null(pars_year)) {
    year <- as.character(year)
    year_hits <- grep(paste0('_', year, '$'), names(pars_year), value = TRUE)
    
    for (nm in year_hits) {
      base_nm <- sub(paste0('_', year, '$'), '', nm)
      pars[[base_nm]] <- pars_year[[nm]]
    }
  }
  
  if (is.null(re_year_t1) && !is.null(year)) {
    re_year_t1 <- as.numeric(as.character(year)) + 1
  }
  
  if (!is.null(re_year_t1) && !is.null(pars_re_year_t1)) {
    re_year_t1 <- as.character(re_year_t1)
    pars$re_b0 <- get_par(pars, 're_b0', 0) +
      get_par(
        pars_re_year_t1,
        paste0('re_u0_year_t1_', re_year_t1), 0)
    pars$re_b1 <- get_par(pars, 're_b1', 0) +
      get_par(
        pars_re_year_t1,
        paste0('re_u1_year_t1_', re_year_t1), 0)
  }
  
  pars
}

surv_lp <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  get_par(pars, 'surv_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_b1', 0) * x +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_b2', 0) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_b3', 0) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_bf', 0) * disturbance
}

sx <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  inv_logit(surv_lp(x, pars, disturbance))
}

grow_mu <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  get_par(pars, 'grow_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_b1', 0) * x +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_b2', 0) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_b3', 0) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_bf', 0) * disturbance
}

grow_sd <- function(x, pars) {
  sqrt(pars$a * exp(pars$b * x))
}

gxy <- function(x, y, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  dnorm(
    y,
    mean = grow_mu(x, pars, disturbance),
    sd = grow_sd(x, pars))
}

# Flowering probability
fl_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  eta <- get_par(pars, 'fl_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_b1', 0) * x +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_b2', 0) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_b3', 0) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_bf', 0) * disturbance
  
  inv_logit(eta)
}


# Flowering-stem number conditional on flowering
fl_n_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  eta <- get_par(pars, 'fln_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 'fln_b1', 0) * x +
    get_par(pars, 'fln_b2', 0) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, 'fln_b3', 0) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, 'fln_bf', 0) * disturbance
  
  exp(eta)
}


# Expected flowering stems per individual
fs_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  fl_x(x, pars, disturbance) * fl_n_x(x, pars, disturbance)
}


# Flowering-stem reference
get_fs_ref <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  if (disturbance == 1) {
    get_par(pars, 'fs_t0_ref_1')
  } else {
    get_par(pars, 'fs_t0_ref_0')
  }
}


# Flowering-stem-to-recruit conversion
re_total_ref <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  re_intercept <- get_par(pars, 're_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 're_bd', 0) * disturbance
  
  re_slope <- get_par(pars, 're_b1', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 're_bf', 0) * disturbance
  
  fs_ref <- get_fs_ref(pars, disturbance)
  
  re_log <- re_intercept + re_slope * log1p(fs_ref)
  
  re_value <- expm1(
    re_log + 0.5 * get_par(pars, 're_sigma', 0)^2)
  
  pmax(re_value, 0)
}


rx <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  fs_value <- fs_x(x, pars, disturbance)
  fs_ref <- get_fs_ref(pars, disturbance)
  re_ref <- re_total_ref(pars, disturbance)
  
  re_per_fs <- re_ref / pmax(fs_ref, .Machine$double.eps)
  
  fs_value * re_per_fs
}


# Recruit size distribution
re_y_dist <- function(y, pars, h = NULL) {
  dens <- dnorm(y, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = pars$recr_sd)
  
  if (!is.null(h)) {
    dens <- dens / sum(dens * h)
  }
  
  dens
}


# Fertility matrix
fyx <- function(y, x, pars, h, disturbance = 0) {
  Pvec <- re_y_dist(y, pars, h = h)
  Rvec <- rx(x, pars, disturbance)
  
  outer(Pvec, Rvec) * h
}

10.6 Kernel: historical size-structured

Code 
kernel <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  S <- sx(y, pars, disturbance = disturbance)
  
  G <- t(outer(
    y, y, Vectorize(function(x, y) {
      gxy(x, y, pars, disturbance = disturbance)
    }))) * h
  
  for (i in 1:n) {
    if (i <= n / 2) {
      G[1, i] <- G[1, i] + 1 - sum(G[, i])
    } else {
      G[n, i] <- G[n, i] + 1 - sum(G[, i])
    }
  }
  
  T <- sweep(G, 2, S, '*')
  
  F <- fyx(
    y = y,
    x = y,
    pars = pars,
    h = h,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  k_yx <- T + F
  
  Imat <- diag(n)
  Zmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  
  K_hist <- rbind(
    cbind(T, F),
    cbind(Imat, Zmat))
  
  list(
    k_yx = k_yx,
    K_hist = K_hist,
    T = T,
    F = F,
    Imat = Imat,
    Zmat = Zmat,
    G = G,
    S = S,
    meshpts = y,
    h = h,
    L = L,
    U = U)
}

lambda_ipm <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  K <- kernel(
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)$K_hist
  
  Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1])
}

10.9 Historical kernel diagnostics by year

Code 
df_hist_kernel_check <- bind_rows(
  lapply(ipm_years, function(year_i) {
    pars_i <- make_ipm_pars(
      pars_mean = pars_all_mean,
      pars_year = pars_all_year,
      pars_re_year_t1 = pars_all_re_year_t1,
      year = year_i,
      re_year_t1 = year_i + 1)
    
    bind_rows(
      lapply(c(0, 1), function(disturbance_i) {
        kern_i <- kernel(
          pars = pars_i,
          disturbance = disturbance_i)
        
        n <- pars_i$mat_siz
        K <- kern_i$K_hist
        
        tibble(
          year = year_i,
          disturbance = disturbance_i,
          n_rows = nrow(K),
          n_cols = ncol(K),
          identity_block = isTRUE(all.equal(
            K[(n + 1):(2 * n), 1:n],
            diag(n))),
          zero_block = all(
            K[(n + 1):(2 * n), (n + 1):(2 * n)] == 0),
          any_nonfinite = any(!is.finite(K)))
      }))
  }))

df_hist_kernel_check

10.10 Observed and projected population growth

Observed growth is calculated from quadrats represented in t - 1, t, and t + 1. Each quadrat is projected with its observed disturbance at year t.

10.10.1 Quadrat-year disturbance lookup

Code 
fire_lookup_quad <- df %>%
  group_by(site, quad, year) %>%
  summarise(
    disturbance_num = first(
      disturbance[!is.na(disturbance)],
      default = NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop')

10.10.2 Quadrat-year abundance

Counts include sized plants and recruits without a usable size measurement.

Code 
df_counts_quad_year <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(site),
    !is.na(quad),
    !is.na(year)) %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    quad,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sized = sum(
      is.finite(logvol_t0),
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unsized_recruits = sum(
      !is.finite(logvol_t0) & recruits == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_ipm_state = n_sized + n_unsized_recruits,
    .groups = 'drop')

10.10.3 Matched consecutive quadrat transitions

Code 
df_obs_pgr_quad <- df_counts_quad_year %>%
  arrange(site, quad, year) %>%
  group_by(site, quad) %>%
  mutate(
    year_tm1 = lag(year),
    n_tm1 = lag(n_ipm_state),
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    n_t1 = lead(n_ipm_state),
    year_gap_prev = year - year_tm1,
    year_gap_next = year_t1 - year) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    year_gap_prev == 1,
    year_gap_next == 1,
    n_ipm_state > 0) %>%
  rename(n_t0 = n_ipm_state) %>%
  left_join(
    fire_lookup_quad,
    by = c('site', 'quad', 'year')) %>%
  filter(!is.na(disturbance_num)) %>%
  mutate(obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0)

10.10.4 Initial quadrat size distribution

Code 
make_initial_n_quad <- function(
    year0,
    site_i,
    quad_i,
    pars) {
  
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  
  breaks <- seq(
    L,
    U,
    length.out = n + 1)
  
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  
  y <- 0.5 *
    (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  df0 <- df %>%
    filter(
      year == year0,
      site == site_i,
      quad == quad_i)
  
  sizes <- df0 %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(logvol_t0)) %>%
    pull(logvol_t0)
  
  size_counts <- hist(
    pmin(
      pmax(sizes, L),
      U),
    breaks = breaks,
    plot = FALSE,
    include.lowest = TRUE)$counts
  
  n_density <- size_counts / h
  
  n_unsized_recruits <- df0 %>%
    summarise(
      n = sum(
        !is.finite(logvol_t0) &
          recruits == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(n)
  
  if (n_unsized_recruits > 0) {
    n_density <- n_density +
      n_unsized_recruits *
      re_y_dist(
        y,
        pars,
        h = h)
  }
  
  n_density
}

10.10.5 Project one quadrat-year

Code 
project_one_quad_year <- function(
    yr,
    site_i,
    quad_i,
    disturbance_y) {
  
  pars_y <- make_ipm_pars(
    pars_mean = pars_all_mean,
    pars_year = pars_all_year,
    pars_re_year_t1 = pars_all_re_year_t1,
    year = yr,
    re_year_t1 = yr + 1)
  
  n_current <- make_initial_n_quad(
    year0 = yr,
    site_i = site_i,
    quad_i = quad_i,
    pars = pars_y)
  
  n_previous <- make_initial_n_quad(
    year0 = yr - 1,
    site_i = site_i,
    quad_i = quad_i,
    pars = pars_y)
  
  n_hist <- c(n_current, n_previous)
  
  K <- kernel(
    pars = pars_y,
    disturbance = disturbance_y)$K_hist
  
  n <- pars_y$mat_siz
  h <- (pars_y$U - pars_y$L) / n
  
  n_initial <- sum(n_current) * h
  
  if (n_initial <= 0) {
    return(
      data.frame(
        year = yr,
        site = site_i,
        quad = quad_i,
        disturbance_num = disturbance_y,
        n_obs_model = n_initial,
        n_proj_model = NA_real_,
        asym_lambda = NA_real_,
        proj_lambda = NA_real_))
  }
  
  n_proj_hist <- as.numeric(K %*% n_hist)
  n_next <- n_proj_hist[1:n]
  n_projected <- sum(n_next) * h
  
  data.frame(
    year = yr,
    site = site_i,
    quad = quad_i,
    disturbance_num = disturbance_y,
    n_obs_model = n_initial,
    n_proj_model = n_projected,
    asym_lambda = Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1]),
    proj_lambda = n_projected / n_initial)
}

10.10.6 Project all matched quadrat transitions

Code 
df_proj_quad <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    seq_len(nrow(df_obs_pgr_quad)),
    function(i) {
      
      project_one_quad_year(
        yr = df_obs_pgr_quad$year[i],
        site_i = df_obs_pgr_quad$site[i],
        quad_i = df_obs_pgr_quad$quad[i],
        disturbance_y = df_obs_pgr_quad$disturbance_num[i])
    }))

10.10.7 Quadrat-level observed and modeled growth

Code 
df_compare_quad <- df_obs_pgr_quad %>%
  left_join(
    df_proj_quad,
    by = c(
      'year',
      'site',
      'quad',
      'disturbance_num')) %>%
  mutate(
    error_asymptotic_vs_obs =
      asym_lambda - obs_pgr,
    error_projected_vs_obs =
      proj_lambda - obs_pgr)

10.10.8 Site-year comparison from matched quadrats

Code 
df_compare_site <- df_compare_quad %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    asym_lambda = weighted.mean(
      asym_lambda,
      w = n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t0 = sum(
      n_t0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t1 = sum(
      n_t1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs_model = sum(
      n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_proj_model = sum(
      n_proj_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_quadrats = n(),
    n_burned_quadrats = sum(
      disturbance_num == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    disturbance_num = as.numeric(
      any(
        disturbance_num == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0,
    proj_lambda = n_proj_model / n_obs_model,
    error_asymptotic_vs_obs =
      asym_lambda - obs_pgr,
    error_projected_vs_obs =
      proj_lambda - obs_pgr)

df_compare_site %>%
  print(
    n = 100,
    width = Inf)

10.10.9 Whole-population annual comparison

Annual totals contain only quadrats represented in t - 1, t, and t + 1.

Code 
df_compare <- df_compare_quad %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    asym_lambda = weighted.mean(
      asym_lambda,
      w = n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t0 = sum(
      n_t0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t1 = sum(
      n_t1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs_model = sum(
      n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_proj_model = sum(
      n_proj_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_quadrats = n(),
    n_sites = n_distinct(site),
    n_burned_quadrats = sum(
      disturbance_num == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    p_burned_quadrats = mean(
      disturbance_num == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    disturbance = if_else(
      any(
        disturbance_num == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE),
      'Fire',
      'No fire'),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0,
    proj_lambda = n_proj_model / n_obs_model,
    disturbance = factor(
      disturbance,
      levels = c(
        'No fire',
        'Fire')))

# Observed vs modeled plot

df_plot <- df_compare %>%
  dplyr::select(year, obs_pgr, asym_lambda, proj_lambda, disturbance) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(asym_lambda, proj_lambda),
    names_to = 'lambda_type',
    values_to = 'lambda') %>%
  mutate(
    lambda_type = recode(
      lambda_type,
      asym_lambda = 'Abundance-weighted asymptotic lambda',
      proj_lambda = 'Projected lambda from observed quadrat size distributions'))

fig_mod_vs_obs <- ggplot(
  df_plot,
  aes(x = lambda, y = obs_pgr, color = disturbance)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, lty = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ lambda_type, scales = 'free_x') +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('No fire' = 'black', 'Fire' = 'red')) +
  labs(
    title = 'Observed population growth vs modeled lambda',
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    x = expression('Modeled ' * lambda),
    y = 'Observed population growth rate',
    color = 'Fire') +
  theme_classic()

11 Yearly historical kuss projection model

11.1 Year-specific environmental-history IPM

This analysis develops a year-specific environmental-history integral projection model (IPM) for Polygala lewtonii. In contrast to the historical population-state model, where the population vector explicitly contains both the current and previous population size distributions, the historical information in this model is carried by the disturbance state.

The timing of disturbance differs among the demographic processes. Survival and growth from year \(t\) to \(t+1\) depend on disturbance during the current interval, denoted \(d_t\). Recruitment from flowering stems in year \(t\) to recruits in year \(t+1\) can also respond to this current disturbance. In contrast, flowering probability and flowering-stem production in year \(t\) depend on disturbance during the preceding interval, denoted \(d_{t-1}\).

The demographic kernel therefore depends on both the current and previous disturbance states:

\[ K_t(d_t,d_{t-1}) = T_t(d_t) + F_t(d_t,d_{t-1}), \]

where \(T_t\) contains survival and growth and \(F_t\) contains recruitment. Survival and growth depend only on current disturbance, while fertility depends on both disturbance states because flowering and flowering-stem production respond to previous disturbance and the flowering-stem-to-recruit transition can respond to current disturbance.

This creates four possible demographic kernels:

\[ K_{00,t}, \qquad K_{10,t}, \qquad K_{01,t}, \qquad K_{11,t}, \]

where the first index represents current disturbance and the second index represents previous disturbance. Thus,

  • \(K_{00,t}\): no fire in either interval,
  • \(K_{10,t}\): fire in the current interval only,
  • \(K_{01,t}\): fire in the previous interval only, and
  • \(K_{11,t}\): fire in both intervals.

11.1.1 One-step projection of the observed population

For the observed annual projection, the historical disturbance state is known. Each quadrat has an observed current disturbance \(d_t\) and previous disturbance \(d_{t-1}\). The appropriate year-specific kernel is therefore selected directly and applied to the observed size distribution in year \(t\):

\[ \mathbf{n}_{t+1} = K_t(d_t,d_{t-1})\mathbf{n}_t. \]

For example, a quadrat that burned during the current interval but did not burn during the preceding interval is projected using

\[ \mathbf{n}_{t+1} = K_{10,t}\mathbf{n}_t. \]

A quadrat that burned in the previous interval but not during the current interval is projected using

\[ \mathbf{n}_{t+1} = K_{01,t}\mathbf{n}_t. \]

Importantly, the previous population vector \(\mathbf{n}_{t-1}\) is not required in this formulation. The reproductive contribution in year \(t\) originates from individuals that are members of the current population \(\mathbf{n}_t\). The historical information required by the model is instead contained in the previous disturbance state \(d_{t-1}\).

The resulting projected annual population growth rate is

\[ \lambda_{\mathrm{proj},t} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{projected},t+1}} {N_{\mathrm{observed},t}}. \]

This projected lambda depends on the observed population structure and the actual disturbance history of each quadrat and can therefore be compared directly with the observed population growth rate from \(t\) to \(t+1\).

11.1.2 Long-term environmental history

The four state-specific kernels can also be examined individually. However, their dominant eigenvalues do not all represent biologically possible long-term disturbance sequences. In particular, repeatedly applying \(K_{10}\) would imply that every year has current fire but no fire in the previous year, while repeatedly applying \(K_{01}\) would imply the opposite. These histories cannot persist because the current disturbance state in one year necessarily becomes the previous disturbance state in the following year.

For long-term population growth, the disturbance history must therefore be updated explicitly. If

\[ p_{j|i} = P(d_t=j \mid d_{t-1}=i), \]

the disturbance process can be represented by transition probabilities between the two environmental states.

The corresponding environmental-history megakernel is

\[ K_{\mathrm{env},t} = \begin{pmatrix} p_{0|0}K_{00,t} & p_{0|1}K_{01,t} \\ p_{1|0}K_{10,t} & p_{1|1}K_{11,t} \end{pmatrix}. \]

The two population blocks represent individuals whose previous disturbance state is no fire or fire. After projection, individuals are automatically transferred into the appropriate disturbance-history state for the following year.

The dominant eigenvalue of this environmental-history kernel provides a long-term growth rate that respects the temporal sequence of disturbance. Thus, the model separates two related questions:

  1. Observed one-step projection: what population growth is predicted from year \(t\) to \(t+1\), given the observed population structure and observed disturbance history?

  2. Environmental-history asymptotic growth: what population growth is expected when the disturbance process continues according to its observed transition probabilities?

# Controls ---------------------------------------------------------------------
ctrl_glmer <- glmerControl(
  optimizer = 'bobyqa',
  optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

ctrl_lmer <- lmerControl(
  optimizer = 'bobyqa',

11.3 Vital rate models

11.3.1 Survival

Code 
# Survival data ----------------------------------------------------------------
df_su <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(survives),
    size_t0 != 0,
    is.finite(logvol_t0),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_2),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_3),
    !is.na(disturbance)) %>%
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    disturbance = factor(disturbance, levels = c(0, 1))) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    id, site, year, size_t0, survives, size_t1,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t1, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3,
    volume_t0, volume_t1, logvol_t0, logvol_t1,
    logvol_t0_2, logvol_t0_3,
    disturbance, stage)

11.3.1.1 Survival model

Code 
mod_su_0 <- glmer(
  survives ~ disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_10 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_11 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_20 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_21 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_30 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + logvol_t0_3 +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_31 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + logvol_t0_3 + disturbance +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)


mods_su <- list(
  mod_su_0, mod_su_10, mod_su_11, 
  mod_su_20, mod_su_21, mod_su_30, mod_su_31)
mods_su_dAIC <- bbmle::AICctab(mods_su, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAIC
mods_su_sorted <- order(mods_su_dAIC)

if (length(v_mod_set_su) == 0) {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- mods_su_sorted[1]
  v_mod_su_index <- mod_su_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_su + 1
  v_mod_su_index <- v_mod_set_su
}

mod_su_best <- mods_su[[mod_su_index_bestfit]]
mod_su_ranef <- coef(mod_su_best)$year

mod_su_best

11.3.1.2 Survival plots by year

Code 
make_su_year_plot <- function(year_i) {
  df_i <- df_su %>% filter(year == year_i)
  
  x <- seq(
    min(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)
  
  pred_i <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    logvol_t0 = x,
    disturbance = levels(df_su$disturbance)) %>%
    mutate(
      logvol_t0_2 = logvol_t0^2,
      logvol_t0_3 = logvol_t0^3,
      disturbance = factor(
        disturbance, levels = levels(df_su$disturbance)),
      year = factor(year_i, levels = levels(df_su$year)))
  
  pred_i$survives <- predict(
    mod_su_best, newdata = pred_i,
    type = "response", re.form = NULL)
  
  pts_i <- df_i %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(logvol_t0, breaks = 8)) %>%
    group_by(bin, disturbance) %>%
    summarise(
      logvol_t0 = mean(logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
      survives = mean(survives, na.rm = TRUE),
      n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(!is.na(logvol_t0), n > 0)
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = pts_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, survives, color = disturbance), size = 1.1) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, survives, color = disturbance,
          linetype = disturbance),
      linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "black", "1" = "red")) +
    labs(
      title = year_i,
      x = expression("log(volume)"[t0]),
      y = expression("Survival probability"[t1])) +
    ylim(0, 1) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 5), legend.position = "none")
}

su_yrs <- lapply(levels(df_su$year), make_su_year_plot)
fig_su_years <- wrap_plots(su_yrs) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = 'Survival - year specific',
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = 'bold'),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9)))

fig_su_years

# including several fairly large individuals and some stage-3 plants.

  filter(
    !is.na(flower),
    is.finite(logvol_t0),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_2),

make_fl_n_year_plot <- function(year_i) {
  df_i <- df_fl_cond %>% filter(year == year_i)
  x <- seq(min(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
           max(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)
  
  pred_i <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    logvol_t0 = x,
    disturbance_prev = levels(df_fl_cond$disturbance_prev)) %>%
    mutate(
      logvol_t0_2 = logvol_t0^2,
      logvol_t0_3 = logvol_t0^3,
      disturbance_prev = factor(
        disturbance_prev, levels = levels(df_fl_cond$disturbance_prev)),
      year = factor(year_i, levels = levels(df_fl_cond$year)))
  
  pred_i <- pred_i %>%
    mutate(
      fl_nr = predict(
        mod_fl_n_best, newdata = pred_i, type = 'response',
        re.form = NULL))
  
  pts_i <- df_i %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(logvol_t0, breaks = 8)) %>%
    group_by(bin, disturbance_prev) %>%
    summarise(
      logvol_t0 = mean(logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
      fl_nr = mean(fl_nr, na.rm = TRUE),
      n = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    filter(!is.na(logvol_t0), n > 0)
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = pts_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, fl_nr, color = disturbance_prev),
      size = 1.1) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, fl_nr, color = disturbance_prev),
      linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c('0' = 'black', '1' = 'red')) +
    labs(
      title = year_i,
      x = expression('log(volume)'[t0]),
      y = 'Number of flowering stems') +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 5), legend.position = 'none')
}

  summarise(

predict_re_safe <- function(model, newdata, re.form = NULL) {
  if (inherits(model, 'merMod')) {
    out <- predict(
      model, newdata = newdata, re.form = re.form, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
  } else {
    out <- predict(model, newdata = newdata)
  }
  return(out)
}

11.4 Parameter extraction

11.4.1 Parameter extraction helpers

Code 
empty_coef_df <- function() {
  data.frame(coefficient = character(), value = numeric())
}

is_mixed_model <- function(model) {
  inherits(model, 'merMod')
}

get_fixef_safe <- function(model) {
  if (is_mixed_model(model)) {
    fixef(model)
  } else {
    coef(model)
  }
}

get_group_coef_safe <- function(model, group_var) {
  if (!is_mixed_model(model)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  coef_list <- coef(model)
  if (!(group_var %in% names(coef_list))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  coef_list[[group_var]]
}

find_model_term <- function(model_terms, aliases) {
  aliases <- unlist(aliases)
  for (alias in aliases) {
    if (grepl('^regex:', alias)) {
      pattern <- sub('^regex:', '', alias)
      hit <- grep(pattern, model_terms, value = TRUE)
    } else {
      hit <- model_terms[model_terms == alias]
    }
    if (length(hit) > 0) {
      return(hit[1])
    }
  }
  NA_character_
}

bind_coef_rows <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!vapply(x, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  out <- do.call(rbind, x)
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

check_duplicate_coefficients <- function(x, object_name = 'parameter table') {
  dup <- x$coefficient[duplicated(x$coefficient)]
  if (length(dup) > 0) {
    stop(
      object_name,
      ' contains duplicated coefficient names: ',
      paste(unique(dup), collapse = ', '))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

coef_df_to_list <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) == 0) {
    return(list())
  }
  check_duplicate_coefficients(x)
  x %>%
    mutate(coefficient = as.character(coefficient)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = coefficient, values_from = value) %>%
    as.list()
}

extract_fixed_pars <- function(model, term_map, fill_missing = TRUE) {
  model_coefs <- get_fixef_safe(model)
  model_terms <- names(model_coefs)
  out <- lapply(names(term_map), function(coef_name) {
    model_term <- find_model_term(model_terms, term_map[[coef_name]])
    if (is.na(model_term)) {
      if (fill_missing) {
        value <- 0
      } else {
        return(NULL)
      }
    } else {
      value <- unname(model_coefs[model_term])
    }
    data.frame(coefficient = coef_name, value = value)
  })
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}

extract_group_pars <- function(model, group_var, term_map, fill_missing = TRUE) {
  coef_matrix <- get_group_coef_safe(model, group_var)
  if (is.null(coef_matrix)) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  model_terms <- colnames(coef_matrix)
  out <- lapply(names(term_map), function(coef_prefix) {
    model_term <- find_model_term(model_terms, term_map[[coef_prefix]])
    if (is.na(model_term)) {
      if (fill_missing) {
        value <- rep(0, nrow(coef_matrix))
      } else {
        return(NULL)
      }
    } else {
      value <- coef_matrix[, model_term]
    }
    data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0(coef_prefix, '_', rownames(coef_matrix)),
      value = value)
  })
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}

extract_re_ranef_devs <- function(model, group_var, group_label) {
  if (!inherits(model, 'merMod')) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  ranef_list <- ranef(model)
  if (!(group_var %in% names(ranef_list))) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  ranef_matrix <- ranef_list[[group_var]]
  out <- list()
  if ('(Intercept)' %in% colnames(ranef_matrix)) {
    out[['intercept']] <- data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0('re_u0_', group_label, '_',
                           rownames(ranef_matrix)),
      value = ranef_matrix[, '(Intercept)'])
  }
  if ('fs_t0_log' %in% colnames(ranef_matrix)) {
    out[['slope']] <- data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0('re_u1_', group_label, '_',
                           rownames(ranef_matrix)),
      value = ranef_matrix[, 'fs_t0_log'])
  }
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}

get_transition_probability <- function(
    disturbance_i,
    disturbance_prev_i) {
  
  df_disturbance_transition %>%
    filter(
      disturbance == disturbance_i,
      disturbance_prev == disturbance_prev_i) %>%
    pull(p_transition)
}
